For \(n\ge 2\),  
\[
a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}\in\{1-1,3-1,1-3,3-3\}=\{0,2,-2,0\}=\{-2,0,2\}.
\]
So only \(a_1=S_1\) can be \(1\) or \(3\); later terms cannot be \(1\) or \(3\). Thus the distinct terms are at most
\[
\{a_1\}\cup\{-2,0,2\},
\]
so at most \(4\) different numbers.

This is achievable, e.g. take partial sums
\[
S_1=1,\ S_2=3,\ S_3=1,\ S_4=1,\ S_5=1,\ldots
\]
Then
\[
a_1=1,\ a_2=2,\ a_3=-2,\ a_4=0,
\]
giving four distinct values.

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
